stem:
A small solenoid of area of cross section 1.6 × 10⁻³ m² is placed inside a larger solenoid of area of cross-section 6.4 × 10⁻³ m², as shown in Fig. 6.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The larger solenoid has 600 turns and is attached to a d.c. power supply to create a magnetic field.

The smaller solenoid has 3000 turns.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Compare the magnetic flux in the two solenoids.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Compare the magnetic flux linkage in the two solenoids.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: State Lenz’s law of electromagnetic induction.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The terminals of the smaller solenoid are connected together. The smaller solenoid is then removed from inside the larger solenoid.

With reference to magnetic fields, explain why a force is needed to remove the smaller solenoid.

figures.caption: Fig. 6.1
figures.alt: A smaller solenoid inside a larger solenoid, with labels giving their cross-sectional areas and numbers of turns, and the larger solenoid connected to a d.c. supply.
